title: Deterministic subnet allocator, SG templates, and conditional Route53 resolver rules for private control plane
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: Private control plane installations require predictable address allocation, repeatable security group policies, and correct cross-account DNS resolution. Current installs leave a lot of address space decisions to operators which causes drift and complex peering rules when we bring up multiple regional control planes. This PR implements: 1) a deterministic subnet allocator that splits a customer-provided VPC CIDR into named controlplane/worker/egress subnets anchored by AZ index so identical cluster manifests produce identical subnet ranges; 2) a set of security-group templates (controlplane, worker-api, egress-proxy, inter-region-peering) exposed as variables so operators can opt in/out to additional stateful ports; 3) conditional Route53 Resolver rules and endpoint automation to forward redwood-internal names (controlplane.redwood.local, datastore.internal.redwood) to customer DNS/IPs or to the VPC endpoints depending on install mode, with clear fallbacks for cross-account peering. The description below is a single continuous string but has logical sections separated by headings and checklists. Changes summary: - Terraform: added modules/network/subnet_allocator.tf, modules/network/sg_templates.tf, modules/dns/route53_resolver_rules.tf, modules/network/az_indexing.tf - Installer: bin/installer/allocate_subnets.py (deterministic allocator used during plan), bin/installer/validate_networking.sh - Helm: charts/redwood-private/values.schema.yaml updated to expose sg template flags - Docs: docs/private-installer/subnets.md, docs/private-installer/dns-forwarding.md - Tests: test/terraform/unit/test_subnet_allocator.go, test/e2e/dns_forwarding_test.sh Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: initial deterministic allocator + unit tests - 2b3c4d5: wire allocator into installer; add CLI flag --seed-for-allocation - 3c4d5e6: SG templates, default port lists and deny-by-default rules - 4d5e6f7: Route53 resolver rule module with cross-account role assumptions - 5e6f7g8: docs and migration notes Why deterministic allocation: When multiple installs are created from the same manifest (e.g. single tenant per region), operators expect deterministic IP placement for firewall rules and peering. The allocator uses the provided VPC CIDR, target number of AZs, and per-AZ index to carve /28-/20 subnets with a stable mapping (algorithm described in docs). Security group templates: Templates are parameterized lists keyed by role. We default to deny-all-ingress/egress and open only the minimal ports needed, with explicit variables to allow wider ranges for legacy customer requirements. Route53 resolver automation: The module creates inbound/outbound endpoints on demand, and conditionally creates resolver rules that forward controlplane.* to 10.0.1.2 (customer DNS) when customer-provided-dns is set, or forwards to aws-vpc-endpoints when private-endpoints-mode is selected. It also adds tags used by the TransitGateway peering automation so resolver rules are discovered across accounts. Backwards compatibility/migration: - Existing installs without the new flag keep current allocations. - A migration tool (bin/installer/migrate_subnets.py) is included to compute and optionally apply the new deterministic allocation; it emits a dry-run report showing differences. Checklist: - [x] deterministic allocator implementation and unit tests - [x] SG templates with examples for common customer profiles - [x] Route53 resolver rules + cross-account role assumption docs - [x] Installer integration + end-to-end e2e test - [x] Docs and upgrade notes Testing notes and reproduction: - Unit tests for allocator cover /16 -> /24 splits and multi-AZ stable mapping. - e2e test spins up a minimal VPC in test-account, creates outbound resolver endpoints, and verifies controlplane.<install>.redwood.local resolves to configured target. - Manual validation steps included in docs/private-installer/dns-forwarding.md What changed in Terraform (illustrative snippets): - modules/network/subnet_allocator.tf: added resource "local_file" "allocation_map" { content = var.allocation_map } - modules/dns/route53_resolver_rules.tf: added aws_route53_resolver_rule "controlplane_forward" { domain_name = "controlplane.redwood.local" rule_type = "FORWARD" resolver_endpoint_id = aws_vpc_endpoint.this.id target_ip { ip = var.customer_dns_ip } } Limitations and open items: - IPv6 deterministic allocation deferred (tracked in ENG-3899) - Resolver rules across non-AWS clouds require additional adapters (future work) Review summary and conversation: - Diego: "Can we ensure the allocator never produces subnets that overlap reserved AWS /100 ranges for AWS-managed services?" Author reply: "Added a reservedRanges variable and pre-flight check; installer will fail early with actionable message." - Maya: "SG defaults look tight; add example allowing existing monitoring ranges." Author: "Added three example profiles (monitoring, pci-legacy, permissive) and documented risks." - Liam: "CI flaked on e2e. Confirmed rerun succeeded and recorded artifact link." CI and checks: - terraform fmt/lint: pass - unit tests: pass - e2e (integration): initial run failed due to quota in sandbox account, rerun after quota increase passed - security scan: pass - package build: pass Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals (Diego + Maya), release-note entry included in docs/internal/release_notes.md Release notes (short): - deterministic subnet allocation for private installs - new SG templates for control-plane and egress profiles - conditional Route53 resolver automation for cross-account DNS forwarding Migration note (short): run bin/installer/migrate_subnets.py --dry-run to preview changes. release_notes: Deterministic subnet allocation for private installs (reduces drift and simplifies peering).
New security-group templates for controlplane/worker/egress with example profiles.
Conditional Route53 Resolver rules to forward internal domains to customer DNS or VPC endpoints.
